ann_return.label: Annualized Return
ann_return.plain: Your compound growth rate scaled to one year. Compounding matters: −50% then +50% is a 25% loss, not zero.

thresholds.verdict: Excellent — beating the market's long-term average
Good — beating your car loan APR
Mediocre — not beating the car loan

ann_return.action: If below 6.0% (car APR), your money does more paying the loan down early.

ann_vol.label: Annualized Volatility
ann_vol.plain: How much the value bounces around in a year — the 'noise' in your returns. Daily σ × √252 because variance scales with time.
ann_vol.action: Your target band is 15–20%. Above that, shift toward BND/SGOV.

sharpe.label: Sharpe Ratio
sharpe.plain: Return earned per unit of total risk, above what T-bills pay. The single most important number in portfolio management.

thresholds.verdict: Bad — you'd be better off in T-bills

sharpe.action: Below 0.3: too much risk for the return — shift to safer allocations (BND/SGOV).

sortino.label: Sortino Ratio
sortino.plain: Like Sharpe, but only penalizes DOWNSIDE volatility — you shouldn't be punished for upside surprises.
sortino.action: Sortino well above Sharpe means your volatility is mostly the good kind.

max_pairwise_corr.label: Max Pairwise Correlation
max_pairwise_corr.plain: The most correlated pair among your holdings. Two assets moving in lockstep give zero diversification benefit.

thresholds.verdict: Above your 80% threshold — essentially the same bet

max_pairwise_corr.action: Above threshold: drop one of the pair or replace with a different sector.

avg_corr.label: Avg Pairwise Correlation
avg_corr.plain: Mean correlation across all pairs of holdings. Lower = the portfolio behaves like more independent bets.
avg_corr.action: Persistently high: run the screener for uncorrelated asset classes.

diversification_ratio.label: Diversification Ratio
diversification_ratio.plain: Weighted average of individual volatilities divided by actual portfolio volatility. 1.0 = no benefit; higher = real risk reduction from mixing assets.

thresholds.verdict: Below your 1.2 minimum — portfolio acts like one asset

diversification_ratio.action: Below minimum: run the screener (--screen) and add the top uncorrelated candidate.

enb.label: Effective # of Bets
enb.plain: How many independent equal-size bets your weights amount to. Equal weights across n assets → n; one dominant holding → toward 1.
enb.action: Dropping over time = concentration drift. Rebalance to restore.

skewness.label: Skewness
skewness.plain: Whether returns lean toward crashes (negative) or spikes up (positive).

thresholds.verdict: Strong crash risk — more dangerous than its volatility suggests

skewness.action: Satellite picks below −0.5 carry hidden crash risk — size them small.

kurtosis.label: Kurtosis
kurtosis.plain: How fat the tails are. 3 = normal bell curve; higher = more extreme days (both directions) than a normal distribution predicts.

thresholds.verdict: Fat tails — extreme days more frequent than normal
Very fat tails — normality-based risk models understate risk

kurtosis.action: Above 5: trust Cornish-Fisher VaR and historic CVaR over plain VaR.

var_hist.label: Historic VaR (5%)
var_hist.plain: On a bad day (worse than 95% of days), how much you could lose. Reported as a positive loss magnitude: 0.021 = lose 2.1%.
var_hist.action: Position-size so a 1-in-20 day stays survivable.

cf_var.label: Cornish-Fisher VaR (5%)
cf_var.plain: VaR adjusted for your actual skewness and fat tails instead of assuming a bell curve. Note: at the 5% level fat tails alone can make this SMALLER than Gaussian VaR — the fat-tail penalty shows up deeper in the tail (1%).

thresholds.verdict: Very risky — skew/tail-aware daily loss above 3%

cf_var.action: Use as your skew-aware daily loss estimate; for tail size use CVaR.

cvar.label: CVaR / Expected Shortfall (5%)
cvar.plain: GIVEN a bad day beyond VaR, the average loss. VaR marks where the danger zone starts; CVaR says how deep it goes. Always worse than VaR.
cvar.action: THE number for position sizing: weight × CVaR = that ticker's tail contribution.

max_drawdown.label: Max Drawdown
max_drawdown.plain: Worst peak-to-trough decline over the period — the 2022 bear market. The window starts at your newest holding's inception (RKLB, 2020-11), so it does NOT include the COVID crash.
max_drawdown.action: Real-time DD beyond 20%: shift equities to SGOV per the CPPI guide.

current_drawdown.label: Current Drawdown
current_drawdown.plain: How far below its all-time peak this position sits right now.

garch_vol_ratio.label: GARCH Vol Ratio
garch_vol_ratio.plain: Tomorrow's forecast volatility vs the last year's average. Volatility clusters — a spike today predicts turbulence tomorrow.
garch_vol_ratio.formula: σ²ₜ₊₁ = ω + α·ε²ₜ + β·σ²ₜ  →  ratio = forecast / historic
garch_vol_ratio.action: REDUCE: pause DCA into this ticker, redirect the month's $ to SGOV until it clears.

garch_signal.label: GARCH Signal
garch_signal.plain: REDUCE when forecast vol exceeds 2× the historical average — historically catches crash onsets without triggering on normal noise.

REDUCE.verdict: Vol spike — pause DCA, redirect to SGOV

egarch_alpha.label: EGARCH Leverage α
egarch_alpha.plain: Asymmetry term: negative means bad news raises volatility more than good news (the leverage effect — normal for equities).

thresholds.verdict: Strong asymmetry — downside shocks amplify hard

egarch_alpha.action: If EGARCH vol ≫ GARCH vol, trust EGARCH — it sees risk GARCH misses.

regime.label: Market Regime
regime.plain: A Markov model sorts recent behavior into Bear / Neutral / Bull states (by mean return and variance). Regimes are sticky — ~85% chance of staying put day to day. Highest-priority signal in the framework.

Bear.verdict: De-risk: pause satellite DCA, redirect to SGOV, recheck weekly

regime.action: Portfolio-level Bear is the strongest danger signal — cut satellite exposure.

p_bear.label: P(Bear)
p_bear.plain: Smoothed probability the asset is currently in the Bear state.
p_bear.action: Watch alongside the hard regime call — a rising P(Bear) leads the flip.

arima_signal.label: ARIMA 5-Day Signal
arima_signal.plain: Statistical forecast of the next 5 days' direction. The weakest model in the framework — barely better than a coin flip, so actions are small.

SELL.verdict: 5-day forecast below −0.2% — halve this month's DCA

arima_signal.action: Fine-tune DCA amounts only; never emergency-sell on ARIMA.

ml_prob.label: ML P(outperform)
ml_prob.plain: XGBoost's probability this ticker beats its own median return over the next 20 trading days, from 16 technical features.
ml_prob.action: Only act when out-of-fold accuracy exceeds 55%.

ml_accuracy.label: ML OOF Accuracy
ml_accuracy.plain: Walk-forward out-of-fold accuracy — honest generalization, with a 20-day embargo between train and test so no future leaks in (audit-fixed).

thresholds.verdict: Marginal — treat as a second opinion
Coin-flipping — ignore this ticker's ML signal

ml_accuracy.action: Gate every ML action on this number.

ml_signal.label: ML Signal
ml_signal.plain: BUY above 60% probability, SELL below 40% — but only trusted when accuracy clears 55%.
ml_signal.action: Supplementary opinion, never the primary signal.

p_beat_target.label: P(beat 8% target)
p_beat_target.plain: Across 5,000 simulated futures, how often you end above your 8%/yr target.

thresholds.verdict: Target unlikely at current risk level

p_beat_target.action: Persistently low with low risk numbers → portfolio is too defensive.

p_beat_hurdle.label: P(beat 6.0% hurdle)
p_beat_hurdle.plain: Probability of out-earning your car loan APR — the bar for investing instead of prepaying the loan.

thresholds.verdict: Coin-flip vs the loan — keep watching
Below 50% — paying the loan down beats investing

p_beat_hurdle.action: Below 50%: shift 5% from BND to equities, or prepay the car instead.

p_loss.label: P(any loss)
p_loss.plain: Probability of ending the horizon below your starting value.

thresholds.verdict: Too aggressive — shift 5% from satellite to BND

p_loss.action: Above 30%: de-risk by moving satellite weight to BND.

p_breach_floor.label: P(breach 15% floor)
p_breach_floor.plain: Probability of losing more than 15% — the outcome your CPPI floor exists to prevent.

thresholds.verdict: Very conservative — room to add satellite risk
DANGER — kill satellite positions, go core-only

p_breach_floor.action: Above 5% is the hard tripwire: cut the satellite bucket (the highest-beta names first) immediately.

ff_alpha.label: FF Alpha (annualized)
ff_alpha.plain: Return left over after accounting for market, size, and value exposure — your genuine edge (or lack of it).
ff_alpha.formula: Rᵢ−Rf = α + β₁(Mkt−Rf) + β₂SMB + β₃HML + ε

thresholds.verdict: Strong alpha — a genuinely good pick
Negative alpha — underperforming its risk exposure

ff_alpha.action: Directional calls need significance too — see the FF Signal.

ff_signal.label: FF Signal
ff_signal.plain: ALPHA_POS/NEG only when the alpha is statistically significant (|t| > 2) AND economically meaningful (|α| > 2%/yr); otherwise NEUTRAL — the sign of an insignificant alpha is noise (audit-fixed).

ALPHA_POS.verdict: Thesis working — pick genuinely beats its factors

ff_signal.action: ALPHA_NEG persisting 2 quarters: replace with a cheaper index ETF.

ff_beta_mkt.label: Market Beta
ff_beta_mkt.plain: Sensitivity to the whole market: 1.0 moves with it, >1.3 amplifies it, <0.7 dampens it.
ff_beta_mkt.action: High-beta satellites need smaller weights for the same portfolio risk.

ff_r2.label: R² (factor-explained)
ff_r2.plain: Share of the ticker's return explained by the three factors. High = it's a market bet, not a stock pick.
ff_r2.action: Informational — pair with alpha to judge the pick.

drift.label: Weight Drift
drift.plain: Gap between a holding's current weight and its blended target (50% strategic plan ⊕ 50% math-optimal MSR).
drift.action: Fix small drift with DCA flows, big drift with trades.

risk_contribution.label: Risk Contribution
risk_contribution.plain: This asset's share of total portfolio variance under the risk-parity weights. Equal Risk Contribution targets 1/n each (cash excluded — including T-bills makes ERC degenerate to ~94% cash).

thresholds.verdict: Equal across non-cash assets by construction

risk_contribution.action: If your ACTUAL weights concentrate risk in one name, trim it.

cppi_floor.label: CPPI Floor
cppi_floor.plain: A ratcheting safety line at 85% of the running PEAK — it rises as you make new highs, locking gains in. Risky allocation = multiplier (3) × cushion above the floor.

thresholds.verdict: Backtest guide, not an automatic trade

cppi_floor.action: In a real crash: compute your cushion, sell down to multiplier × cushion.

cppi_breached.label: Floor Breached
cppi_breached.plain: Whether the backtest ever fell through the floor.

yes.verdict: Breached — raise floor to 90% or drop multiplier to 2

cppi_breached.action: Breach = your parameters are too loose for this portfolio's volatility.

glide_equity.label: Glidepath Equity %
glide_equity.plain: Time-based de-risking: equities glide linearly from 85% to 60% over 36 months as the car-loan horizon approaches.

thresholds.verdict: Follow the month's split when DCAing

glide_equity.action: Anchored at your invest_start_date — confirm it in Settings.

div_score.label: Diversification Score
div_score.plain: Candidate ranking: 50% low correlation to your portfolio, 30% Sharpe, 20% smaller max drawdown.

thresholds.verdict: Strong candidate — low correlation + decent returns
Moderate — consider if you need diversification
Weak — too correlated or poor risk/return

div_score.action: If DR < 1.2 or max corr > 0.80: add the top scorer, drop the most-correlated holding.

severity.label: Action Severity
severity.plain: Aggregated urgency across all signals in priority order: Regime > GARCH > ML (accuracy-gated) > FF > ARIMA.

normal.verdict: All signals normal — continue the plan

danger.verdict: Primary signal fired — pause/redirect DCA now

severity.action: Follow each card's specific instruction; danger overrides everything below it.

sgov_redirect.label: SGOV Redirect
sgov_redirect.plain: Dollars pulled from paused/reduced tickers this month, parked in 0–3-month Treasuries until their danger signals clear.

thresholds.verdict: Money stays invested — just in the safe bucket

sgov_redirect.action: Resume normal DCA when the source ticker's signal clears.

period_return.label: Window Return
period_return.plain: Total price return over the selected window (not annualized). The Trends default window starts one year before your invest start date.

thresholds.verdict: Down hard — check the drawdown and regime chips

period_return.action: Trend context for DCA timing — pair with regime and GARCH before acting.

pct_from_52w_high.label: % Below 52-Week High
pct_from_52w_high.plain: How far the latest price sits under its highest close of the past year. 0% = at the high.

thresholds.verdict: Deep below the high — either a discount or a downtrend; check regime

pct_from_52w_high.action: A big gap with a Bull regime can be a DCA opportunity; with Bear, it's a falling knife.

sma_state.label: Moving-Average Trend
sma_state.plain: Position of the 20-day vs 50-day moving average — the classic trend gauge the ML features also use. A golden cross (20d rising through 50d) marks emerging uptrends; a death cross the reverse.
sma_state.action: Trend confirmation only — the framework never trades on crossovers alone.

rolling_vol.label: Rolling Volatility (60d)
rolling_vol.plain: Annualized volatility over a trailing 60-day window — shows risk-regime shifts long before they hit the full-period number.

thresholds.verdict: Turbulent — expect GARCH to flag REDUCE if it persists

rolling_vol.action: Rising strips across many tickers = market-wide stress building.

rolling_sharpe.label: Rolling Sharpe (60d)
rolling_sharpe.plain: Risk-adjusted return over a trailing 60-day window. Noisy by nature — read the level and direction, not single wiggles.

thresholds.verdict: Losing on a risk-adjusted basis lately

rolling_sharpe.action: Persistent negative rolling Sharpe on a satellite = replacement-watch.

rebased_perf.label: Rebased Performance
rebased_perf.plain: Every line starts at 100 at the window start, so slopes compare growth directly regardless of price level. The portfolio line blends all holdings at target weights.
rebased_perf.action: Click legend entries to isolate lines; laggards vs the portfolio line are DCA-review candidates.

scenario_profile.label: Risk Profile
scenario_profile.plain: Three candidate allocations: Conservative = your plan blended 50/50 with the minimum-volatility portfolio; Current = your strategic plan; Aggressive = your plan blended 50/50 with the max-Sharpe portfolio. Blending respects both the math and your diversification thesis (§15).

aggressive.verdict: Tilted toward MSR — highest expected risk-adjusted return

scenario_profile.action: Each cell lists the exact trades to move there.

expected_value.label: Expected Value
expected_value.plain: Mean terminal wealth across seeded Monte Carlo simulations at this horizon for this allocation.

thresholds.verdict: An average across thousands of futures — pair with P(loss)

expected_value.action: Compare cells in a row to see what extra risk buys at each horizon.

weighted_er.label: Weighted Expense Ratio
weighted_er.plain: The blended annual fee of the whole book — each fund's expense ratio times its weight. It is the only number on this page that is guaranteed: you pay it every year, in every market, win or lose.

thresholds.verdict: Fine — the satellites are paying for themselves
Getting expensive — the tilt has to earn the fee
Above your 0.60% limit — fees eat the edge

weighted_er.action: Between two funds with the same exposure, take the cheaper one (XAR 0.35% vs ITA 0.40%; ROKT 0.45% vs ARKX 0.75%). RKLB is a single stock and carries no ER.

fund_corr_to_port.label: Correlation to the Rest of the Book
fund_corr_to_port.plain: How tightly this fund moves with everything else you hold, that fund excluded. Low is the entire point of owning it — 0.9 means you bought the same bet twice under a new ticker.

thresholds.verdict: Genuine diversifier — moves on its own
Overlapping — most of this risk is already in the book

fund_corr_to_port.action: A swap only pays if the replacement's correlation to the rest is materially lower AND its standalone Sharpe is not materially worse.

composite_score.label: Composition Score
composite_score.plain: The composition review's ranking composite. Meaningless in absolute terms — only its distance from your CURRENT portfolio's score matters.

thresholds.verdict: Compare against the CURRENT bar — a build below it is rejected by construction

composite_score.action: Weight the structural inputs (DR, ER, P(floor)) over the sample-dependent Sharpe — past-window Sharpe ranks are noisy.

deploy_return_range.label: Return Range (per year)
deploy_return_range.plain: Low · base · high yearly return for this bucket, from YOUR inputs. Base is the honest middle; low and high are a bad and a good version of the same deal, not the worst and best imaginable.

thresholds.verdict: Compare buckets on the BASE number, then look at how far LOW falls

deploy_return_range.action: A wide range is the risk. If you could not live with the low case, shrink the bucket rather than hoping for the base case.

deploy_vs_hurdle.label: Versus Your Hurdle
deploy_vs_hurdle.plain: Your hurdle is the return you could get with no effort and little risk — paying down a loan, or a Treasury bill. Money should only leave it for something expected to beat it.

clears.verdict: Beats the hurdle even in the low case

likely.verdict: Beats it on the base case, not the low case

misses.verdict: Below the hurdle on the base case

deploy_vs_hurdle.action: A bucket that misses is taking risk or effort for less than the safe option pays. Fix the assumptions or move the money.

deploy_risk.label: Risk Level
deploy_risk.plain: How likely this is to lose money, on one scale for every kind of asset so a flip and a fund can sit side by side.

1.verdict: Very low — insured cash, Treasuries, paying off debt

2.verdict: Low — bonds, CDs past the insurance limit

3.verdict: Medium — diversified stocks, a financed rental

4.verdict: High — a flip, a single stock, a leveraged deal

5.verdict: Very high — can go to zero: startups, private deals

deploy_risk.action: Each type starts at a sensible level; change it under More assumptions when your deal is safer or riskier than typical.

deploy_liquidity.label: Time To Get Cash Back
deploy_liquidity.plain: How long it takes to turn this back into spendable money without taking a beating. The thing people underestimate most after a win.

weeks.verdict: A few weeks of notice or settlement

months.verdict: Needs a sale: listing, buyer, closing

locked.verdict: No exit until the deal ends

deploy_liquidity.action: Anything you might need within a year belongs in a 'days' bucket.

deploy_effort.label: Your Time
deploy_effort.plain: Hours of your own life each month. A return that needs a second job is partly a wage, not an investment return.

full.verdict: A second job — about 80 hours a month

deploy_effort.action: Price your time: subtract what those hours are worth before comparing against a hands-off bucket.

deploy_concentration.label: Biggest Bucket
deploy_concentration.plain: The share of the allocated money sitting in the single largest bucket. One deal going wrong should not undo the win.

thresholds.verdict: Most of the money rides on one outcome

deploy_concentration.action: Above the warning line, ask what happens to the plan if this one bucket has its low case.

deploy_illiquid_share.label: Hard To Reach
deploy_illiquid_share.plain: The share of the allocated money that would take months or longer to get back.

thresholds.verdict: More than half is tied up
Nearly all of it is tied up

deploy_illiquid_share.action: Keep an emergency fund and any money due for taxes on the win OUTSIDE the tied-up buckets.

deploy_end_value.label: Projected Value
deploy_end_value.plain: What the allocated money becomes by your horizon. Each bucket earns its own rate until it finishes, then your reinvest rate. The low and high figures are bookends — every bucket having its bad (or good) case at once — not a forecast range.

thresholds.verdict: Compare against the hurdle line: what the same money makes doing the safe thing

deploy_end_value.action: If base is barely above the hurdle value, the plan is taking risk for little extra.
